articles.title: A meeting appears at the wrong time after travelling

steps.text: Open the same invitation in your work web calendar.
Compare the time zone shown in the invitation with the one displayed on the calendar view.
Confirm the start time and time zone with the organizer before proposing a new time.
Compare the start time and zone in the original invitation with the stored event and its web view. (Expected: The stored start time matches the organizer's invitation.)
Check the time zone label used by the affected calendar client and compare the converted time for that date. (Expected: The apparent difference matches the selected display zone.)

Guide the employee through the supported calendar display preference after confirming the intended zone with them. (Expected: The view displays the stored event at the intended local time without changing the invitation.)

articles.verify: The affected calendar and the organizer's invitation agree after converting both times to the same time zone.
articles.escalate_when: The same time zone shows different start times, or the stored event differs from the invitation.

articles.title: How to share my work calendar with a coworker

steps.text: Open your work calendar in webmail and select Share on your own calendar.
Enter your coworker's company address and confirm the address shown.
Select Can view when I'm busy and send the invitation.
Ask the coworker to open your calendar and confirm they see your availability.
Confirm that the employee owns the selected calendar and the recipient is an eligible company account. (Expected: The share is for the intended calendar and coworker.)
Have the employee review the permission list and select availability only for that recipient. (Expected: The entry grants busy and free visibility only.)
Check the calendar from the recipient's side with a test event that contains no real meeting details. (Expected: The recipient sees the time block and cannot see the test event's details.)

articles.verify: The coworker can open the shared calendar and sees availability without event titles.
articles.escalate_when: The sharing button is unavailable, sharing fails for an eligible coworker, or the recipient can see more than the selected permission allows.

articles.title: A cancelled repeating meeting still appears for some attendees

steps.text: Verify the cancellation with the organizer and collect the event identifier, series identifier, affected date and attendee list through restricted diagnostics. (Expected: The cancelled occurrence or series is identified without relying on its title.)
Compare organizer and attendee copies in webmail and check delivery of the cancellation update. (Expected: The affected mailbox has a stale record or missed the update.)

With the organizer's approval, use the supported calendar repair workflow for the affected event ID and scope. (Expected: The stale entry is cleared without altering active occurrences or unrelated events.)
Ask an affected attendee and a control attendee to refresh the calendar and compare the next valid occurrence. (Expected: The cancelled entry is absent and valid meetings are still present.)

articles.verify: The cancelled occurrence is gone from affected attendees' web calendars and valid future occurrences still appear.
articles.escalate_when: The owner cannot confirm the scope, several unrelated series are affected, or the stale event returns after repair.

articles.title: Password reset link says it has expired

steps.text: Start one new reset from the known Company Login page.
Open the newest reset message you just requested and use it promptly.
Close the older reset messages and return to the normal sign-in page after the reset.
Compare reset issuance and redemption timestamps for the employee's account without collecting the reset URL. (Expected: The failed request maps to an expired, superseded or consumed token.)
Initiate one reset through the verified account workflow if the employee cannot issue one. (Expected: A fresh token is associated with the correct account and sent through the approved channel.)
Have the employee open the newest message privately and confirm the completion event. (Expected: One token is redeemed successfully and the newer password is active.)

articles.verify: The employee signs in from the usual page with the new password.

Guide the employee to the known Company Login page and have them complete identity verification privately. (Expected: The recovery flow accepts the employee's registered method.)

When self-service is unavailable, verify identity through the approved process and initiate a one-time reset through the approved channel. (Expected: The employee completes the reset privately and the audit event shows success.)

articles.verify: The employee signs in to Company Login with the new password and reaches the work home page.
articles.escalate_when: The account is locked, no recovery method is available, or the reset succeeds but the sign-in still fails.

articles.title: Password reset offers a recovery phone I can no longer use

articles.title: The work computer quarantined a file opened from an attachment

steps.text: Don't click anything else, and disconnect from the network if asked
Contact the help desk from a separate trusted device and report the alert time and computer name.
Leave the file quarantined and tell support whether you opened it before the alert appeared.

Match the device and timestamp to the endpoint security event and preserve the relevant file identifier, process trail and action status. (Expected: A genuine endpoint alert and the quarantine outcome are confirmed.)

Review execution and connection telemetry for the time around the alert, then have Security isolate the device through the approved workflow if indicated. (Expected: The review determines likely execution and contains confirmed exposure.)
Search approved mail and endpoint telemetry for the same file identifier and sender indicators. (Expected: Related deliveries and endpoints are linked to the incident.)
Have Security direct remediation and check the endpoint again before restoring normal use. (Expected: Required remediation is recorded and no active detection remains.)

articles.verify: Security confirms the quarantined file is contained, evaluates any execution and clears the device for normal work.
articles.escalate_when: Escalate on receipt. Flag urgently if the attachment ran, quarantine failed, or the same indicator appears on other devices.

articles.title: Internet is slow only when this computer uses a network cable

steps.text: Check that the accessible cable ends are seated firmly if the desk has a directly connected network cable.
Use the approved office Wi-Fi for work if it is available.
Tell support which desk and cable you were using and whether Wi-Fi worked normally.
Check the active link speed and port error counters during a transfer from the affected desk. (Expected: The wired link is below its expected speed or accumulates physical errors.)
Replace the suspect patch cable with a known-good approved cable on the same port and repeat the transfer. (Expected: The link negotiates the expected speed and errors stop increasing.)

Compare the wired transfer with a healthy reference port and record the faulty cable in the ticket. (Expected: Both wired connections perform in the expected range and the faulty cable is removed from use.)

articles.verify: With Wi-Fi out of the test path, the desk's wired connection opens approved pages normally and link errors do not increase.
articles.escalate_when: The replacement cable shows the same errors, multiple desks are affected, or the switch port cannot establish a stable link.

articles.title: Office Wi-Fi rejects a laptop after its network certificate expired

steps.text: Locate the affected device's wireless authentication attempts and verify the failure reason and certificate validity. (Expected: The device is rejected for an expired client certificate.)

Attach the device to an approved managed wired connection and check its enrollment and certificate renewal status. (Expected: Endpoint management can reach the device and identifies any pending renewal failure.)
Use the managed certificate renewal workflow and verify it issued a valid credential for that device. (Expected: The office Wi-Fi profile can select the new certificate.)
Reconnect to the approved office network and check authentication and address assignment. (Expected: The renewed certificate is accepted and the device receives a valid network address.)

articles.verify: The laptop reconnects to office Wi-Fi and opens an authorized work page after the cable is disconnected.
articles.escalate_when: Renewal fails, the new certificate is rejected, or certificates expire on multiple managed devices.

articles.title: Company Website opens but images load slowly for first-time visitors

steps.text: Capture cold and repeat load timings for a representative public page using approved external probes. (Expected: Delay is concentrated in image requests during cold loads while the page itself responds promptly.)

Inspect response headers and edge metrics for the slow image paths and compare them with an unaffected image. (Expected: Slow paths miss or bypass the shared cache and show longer upstream response times.)

Have the site owner review the affected image paths for public eligibility and deploy the approved cache configuration for those assets only. (Expected: Eligible public images are served by the cache after the first fill.)
Test from clean browser sessions and separate locations and compare image timings with baseline. (Expected: Cold page loads meet the expected timing and image content is correct.)

articles.verify: A first-time visit from multiple external test locations loads the affected images within the site's expected time.
articles.escalate_when: Cold loads remain slow, cache rules appear to include private assets, or the homepage starts failing outright.

articles.title: Company Website is down for customers with a certificate warning

steps.text: Use approved independent external probes to check the certificate served for the production hostname at multiple edge locations. (Expected: The probes see the expired certificate and identify which endpoints serve it.)

Compare the deployed certificate fingerprint, hostname and expiration with the managed certificate inventory. (Expected: The failed production certificate and intended valid replacement are identified.)

Have the Company Website owner deploy the approved replacement certificate and chain through the standard edge workflow. (Expected: The edge locations begin presenting the correct valid certificate for the hostname.)
Repeat HTTPS checks from independent networks and open representative public pages through a normal browser. (Expected: Trust verification passes and pages open without a certificate warning.)

articles.verify: The public homepage and a representative secondary page open over HTTPS from separate external networks without a warning.
articles.escalate_when: Escalate immediately with more than one user affected or when independent external probes confirm an invalid production certificate.
